text:
maria_finance: Quick finance broadcast: temporary p-card monthly cap for Q2 (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) set to $1,500 per employee. This is a short-term cashflow measure while we finalize Dedicated capacity commitments and year-end vendor payment terms. Please read below for exceptions & next steps. :loudspeaker:

emma_sales: Oof — does this affect client travel or deal-related spend?

maria_finance: Client travel is exempt (use the Travel card flow). Deal-related spend that is pre-approved in SFDC and tagged to a closed-won opportunity is exempt too, but please attach the opportunity link in the purchase request.

dan_procure: If someone needs to make a >$1,500 purchase for onboarding (one-time), what's the path?

maria_finance: For one-offs between $1,500 and $5,000: submit the purchase form and select "manager + procurement" approval route. For one-offs > $5,000 or recurring commitments, procurement will require a PO and finance director sign-off. We recommend starting vendor-add early (see link).

procurement-bot: :robot_face: Reminder: submit here for manager+procurement approvals: https://redwood.internal/forms/purchase-request. New flag for Q2 cap: `q2-pcard-cap-2026`. Auto-routing will add a "rush-review" if the vendor is new.

ryan_ops: How does this interact with Dedicated GPU pool commitments? Those are multi-month and typically >$20k.

maria_finance: Dedicated commitments are handled via the Vendor Contract flow (Procurement + Finance + Legal). Do NOT use p-cards for Dedicated capacity. Steps: 1) open Vendor Request > include expected monthly spend, contract term, and model of commitment (reserved vs burst). 2) Procurement creates PO and routes to Finance for allocation. 3) Ops schedules provisioning after PO signed. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/procurement/dedicated-contracts

emma_sales: Timeline for relaxing cap?

maria_finance: Plan is to reassess mid-June. If cashflow improves and vendor PO queue is clear, we'll lift early. We'll post an update in #finance with a 48h heads-up before changes.

maria_finance: Exceptions process (quick sample to paste into the form):

```
requester: emma_sales
vendor: Conferly Events
amount: 2500
reason: client dinner for deal close (tagged opp: OP-1234)
requested_approvers: manager, procurement
notes: travel-exempt check performed
```

maria_finance: A couple of operational notes: - Single-use virtual cards remain allowed but will be subject to the $1,500 cap per employee for non-exempt categories. - Default GL mapping for p-card spend remains `5410_SaaS` for SaaS subscriptions and `5490_Other` for one-off hardware/tools; procurement will reclassify large invoices during PO processing.

dan_procure: We'll add a shortcut in the procurement form to attach the SFDC opportunity and invoice templates.

procurement-bot: :white_check_mark: New workflow tag enabled: `q2-pcard-cap-2026`. Use the form above; missing cost center will auto-reject.

maria_finance: TL;DR: Q2 temp p-card cap $1,500/month per employee (exempt: travel & approved deal spend); $1.5k-$5k = manager+procurement; >$5k or recurring = PO + finance director. Dedicated capacity NEVER on p-card. Reassess mid-June; ping me for edge cases. :calendar:
